text:
Matt: Heads-up — saw a p99 spike during the last burst (approx 09:43–09:52 UTC). Throughput stayed fine but tail shot up ~3x :eyes:
Anya: link to profiling? flamegraph? :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Matt: uploaded a short perf dump to s3: s3://redwood-perf/1805321110/pdump.txt.gz
Matt: quick summary from the top: kernel-selector chose fallback generic kernel for ~22% of requests during the spike, KV cache miss rate jumped to 0.72, microbatch sizes were trended to 28 avg (target 32)
Rahul: interesting — fallback -> generic kernel explains latency. selector logs usually show why: probably model seq len distribution shifted and optimized kernels had no matching fast-path. Can you paste the selector log lines?
Matt: pasted snippet:
```
[09:45:12] kernel-selector: candidate kernels=[fused_attn_fast, attn_opt_v2] scores=[0.72, -inf] selected=generic_attn
[09:45:12] reason=kv_miss_penalty(0.48) + batching_profile(0.33) -> generic_attn
```
Rahul: kv_miss_penalty looks high. If KV cache was cold or invalidated then scoring pushes away from optimized kernels. Sasha, any infra events around cache eviction?
Sasha: autoscaler scaled from 8 -> 18 nodes at 09:44 (burst). We saw a KS cache shard rebalance and a couple of warmup failures. kv_preheat didn't finish for new pods before traffic hit. infra-bot posted the scale event: autoscaler.scale_up nodepool=runtime-burst delta=10
Anya: so two effects colliding: (1) new pods w/ cold KV cache -> cache miss penalty and (2) kernel selector fallback because batching profile changed during scale-up -> p99 up. Tradeoff: larger microbatch helps throughput but increases per-request queuing tail when some kernels are slower.
Matt: our microbatch target currently 32, but observed microbatch actual avg 28 -> suggests batching backpressure when capacity churns. Lowering to 16 would reduce queuing latency but hurt peak throughput. Thoughts on A/B?
Rahul: propose two experiments: A) microbatch_target=16 + aggressive kv_preheat=true for burst nodes; B) keep 32 but change selector to tolerate higher kv_miss_rate by lowering kv_miss_penalty weight (temp). Run both on canary pool. Measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
Sasha: to add: adjust autoscaler behavior — increase prewarm target and add a short "hold" after scale-up to let kv_preheat finish before routing full traffic. That should reduce cold misses. Also we can enable kernel pinning for canary to prefer fused_attn_fast for 30s after it warms.
Anya: what about quantization fallback? any regresses there? Matt: not in this spike; all traces show same quant path. Only attn kernel fallback.
Matt: quick perf numbers from the window (09:42–09:50): p50=42ms, p95=180ms, p99=520ms (baseline p99 ~170ms).
Rahul: rough cost tradeoff: lowering microbatch to 16 increases GPU utilization inefficiency ~12% but drops p99 by ~40% in sim. Prewarm adds small steady cost but avoids large tail.
Matt: action items:
- Rahul: run kernel-selector weight test (kv_miss_penalty -> 0.6x) on canary cluster for 6h, collect p95/p99/tokens/s (assigned)
- Sasha: increase prewarm pool for burst nodes + add 30s hold before full weight, coordinate with autoscaler (assigned)
- Anya: run microbatch_target=16 A/B test on 5% traffic with detailed tracing (assigned)
- Matt: collect combined dashboards and check whether p99 drop outweighs throughput loss; target decision by tomorrow EOD
Anya: quick config snippet for tests:
```
runtime.config {
  microbatch_target: 16 # canary
  kv_preheat: true
  kernel_selector {
    kv_miss_penalty: 0.6 # experiment
    pin_warm_kernel_seconds: 30
  }
  autoscaler {
    prewarm_count: 4
    post_scale_hold_seconds: 30
  }
}
```
Sasha: I'll coordinate the autoscaler change with infra and post the rollout window. Aim for 1h ramp tomorrow morning during low-cost window.
infra-bot: scale_op recorded: planned_prewarm=4, canary_pool=on, owner=sasha
Matt: thanks — let's keep messages short here. If anyone sees another regression elsewhere tag me. :thumbsup:
Rahul: +1. Will post initial results in this thread.
Anya: adding a quick note — when we run the microbatch change, include KV hit-rate and selector decision histograms in the dashboard so we can tie causality.
Matt: good call. end.
